title: Basics of Computer
summary: A computer is a device that transforms data into meaningful information. It can accept data, store data, process data as desired, retrieve stored data when required and print the result in the desired format. Its major characteristics are high speed, accuracy, diligence, versatility and storage. Computer components are of two kinds: hardware (the machine and its connected devices) and software (the programs that make the hardware work).

Every computer performs five basic operations: input, storage, processing, output and control (the Input–Process–Output cycle). (1) Input unit — enters data and programs into the computer. (2) Control Unit (CU) — supervises input, output, processing and storage; decides when to start and stop receiving data and where to store it; takes care of step-by-step processing. (3) Memory unit — stores data and instructions. (4) Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) — performs addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, logic and comparison. (5) Output unit — produces results from the data as useful information. The ALU and CU together form the Central Processing Unit (CPU), the 'brain' of the computer.
Peripheral devices are connected to the computer externally to perform specific functions: input devices, output devices and other peripherals.

Input devices accept data and instructions from the user. Keyboard — the most common input device; the usual layout is QWERTY and a standard keyboard has 104 keys (cursor keys are duplicated on the numeric pad). Mouse — an electro-mechanical hand-held pointing device used to select menu commands, move icons, resize windows, start programs ('point and click'); older mice use a ball, newer ones are optical/laser. Light pen — a light-sensitive pointer used to select objects by pointing directly at the screen. Optical scanner — automatic data collection that removes manual input; a bar-code reader is a special image scanner; an OCR (Optical Character Recognition) device, used by banks, converts a scanned printed page into editable text. Touch screen — input given by touching buttons on the screen. Microphone — takes voice as input; desktop and hand-held types. Track ball — a 'mouse lying on its back'; the ball is rolled with the thumb or fingers; it is stationary, needs little space and is popular on portable computers.

Output devices return processed data (information) to the user. Monitor (Visual Display Unit) — the most important output device. CRT (Cathode Ray Tube) monitors use a large vacuum tube like an old TV; LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) monitors are flat panel monitors and are popular today. Resolution is measured in pixels (800 × 600, 1024 × 768, 1280 × 1024).

Printers give a hard copy (printout). Laser printer — high quality, very fast and quiet, used in publishing; up to 200 pages per minute in black and white and 100 in colour. Ink-jet printer — sprays ink through up to 64 tiny nozzles; good quality, quiet, not very fast; costs about half a laser printer. Dot matrix printer — the print head hits the paper through a ribbon and forms characters with dots; cheap and versatile but noisy, slow and lower quality; speed is measured in characters per second (CPS). Line printer — used with large computers for text reports; 100 to 3800 lines per minute.

Plotter — produces large drawings such as building plans and machine blueprints using coloured pens moved by a robotic arm; it draws curves as many short straight lines. Two designs: flat bed (small, kept on a table, limited paper size) and drum (big, uses rolls of paper of unlimited length). Speakers — output devices that let you listen to music and voice.

A program is a set of instructions given in a particular sequence; software is a set of programs that makes the hardware perform tasks in a particular order. Software is of two main types: system software and application software.

System software runs the computer, controls its operations and manages its resources. When the computer is switched on, the programs stored in ROM are executed and make the computer ready to work — this set of programs is system software. The operating system (OS) is system software that provides an interface between the user and the computer, manages hardware devices and disk file systems and supports application programs; examples are UNIX, Windows and Linux. Utilities are system software that bridge the gap between the OS and users' needs — compress (zip)/uncompress files, antivirus, split and join files.

Application software is a set of programs written for specific tasks, such as a library information system or a student information system. (a) Generalized packages are user-friendly software for general needs: word processing (WordPerfect, MS-Word, OpenOffice.org Writer), spreadsheets (Lotus Smart Suite, MS-Excel, OpenOffice.org Calc, Apple Numbers), presentations (MS-PowerPoint, OpenOffice.org Impress), databases (MS-Access, MS-SQL Server, ORACLE) and graphics (Paint Shop Pro, Adobe Photoshop). (b) Customized packages are developed for the specific needs of an organisation, such as payroll, inventory control or student details, using high-level languages.

Every computer language has rules called its SYNTAX. Low-level languages are close to the machine: (a) machine language — 0s and 1s (binary), understood directly by the computer, machine dependent and difficult to write; (b) assembly language — uses symbolic codes called mnemonics instead of 0s and 1s; easier than machine language but still machine dependent.

High-level languages use English-like statements, are machine independent and easy to program: BASIC (Beginners All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code — easy, general purpose), COBOL (Common Business Oriented Language — commercial applications), FORTRAN (Formula Translation — mathematical and scientific problems), C (structured programming for all purposes) and C++ (object-oriented, general purpose).

A compiler is software that reads a program written in a high-level language and translates it into an equivalent machine-language program. The programmer's program is called the source program and the translated program produced by the compiler is the object program. An assembler translates a program written in assembly language into machine language.

vsa: What is a memory unit? What does it do?

The memory unit is the part of the computer that stores data and instructions. It holds the data before and after processing so that the CPU can use it, and results can be retrieved whenever required.
April 2026
What is computer organisation?

Computer organisation is the way the parts of a computer are arranged to work together. A computer has an input unit, a memory unit, a control unit, an arithmetic logic unit and an output unit; it accepts input, stores and processes it under the control unit and gives output.
April 2026
What are hardware and software?

Hardware is the physical machine and its connected devices, such as the monitor, keyboard and mouse. Software is a set of programs that makes the hardware perform tasks in a particular order, for example Windows or MS-Word.

or: What is the function of a mouse?
A mouse is a hand-held pointing device. It moves the pointer on the screen and is used to select menu commands, move icons, resize windows, start programs and choose options by 'point and click'.

vsa: Give the difference between a mouse and a track ball.

A mouse is moved across a flat surface to move the pointer. A track ball is like a mouse lying on its back: it stays still and the ball is rolled with the thumb or fingers, so it needs little space and can be used on any surface — popular on portable computers.

or: Differentiate between a plotter and a printer.

A printer gives hard copies of documents and pictures on normal paper sizes. A plotter is designed to draw large drawings such as building plans and blueprints using pens moved by a robotic arm; it draws curves as many short straight lines.

vsa: What are utility software? Give examples.

Utilities are system software that bridge the gap between the operating system and the needs of users. Examples: compress (zip)/uncompress (unzip) software, antivirus software, and split and join files software.

sa: What is a keyboard? Describe its various types of keys.

A keyboard is the most common input device, used to type letters, numbers and symbols; the common layout is QWERTY with about 104 keys. Types of keys: (1) alphanumeric (typing) keys — letters, numbers and symbols; (2) function keys F1–F12 for special tasks; (3) cursor control (arrow) keys plus Home, End, Page Up and Page Down; (4) the numeric keypad; (5) special keys such as Enter, Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Tab, Backspace, Delete and Esc.
What is the difference between system software and application software? Give examples.

System software runs and controls the computer and manages its resources; it works in the background and supports other programs — e.g. operating systems (Windows, Linux, UNIX) and utilities (antivirus, zip). Application software is written to do a specific task for the user — e.g. MS-Word for documents, MS-Excel for calculations, or a payroll package. Application software needs system software to run.

or: Differentiate between low-level and high-level languages with examples.

Low-level languages are close to the machine: machine language (0s and 1s) and assembly language (mnemonics). They are machine dependent and hard to learn. High-level languages use English-like statements, are machine independent and easy to program, e.g. BASIC, COBOL, FORTRAN, C and C++. High-level programs need a compiler to be translated into machine language.

sa: What are compilers? Why are they needed? What are the programs before and after translation called?

A compiler is software that reads a program written in a high-level language and translates it into an equivalent program in machine language. It is needed because the computer understands only machine language (0s and 1s). The program written by the programmer is the source program; the program produced after translation is the object program.
What is application software? Explain its types with examples.

Application software is a set of programs written to perform specific tasks for users. (1) Generalized packages cater to general needs: word processing (MS-Word), spreadsheets (MS-Excel), presentations (PowerPoint), databases (MS-Access, ORACLE) and graphics (Adobe Photoshop). (2) Customized packages are developed for the specific needs of an organisation, such as payroll, inventory control or student information systems.
What are optical scanners? Briefly describe bar-code readers and OCR devices.

Optical scanners collect data automatically and remove manual typing; an image scanner translates printed images into electronic form that can be stored and edited. A bar-code reader is a special scanner that reads bar codes on products. An OCR (Optical Character Recognition) device, used by banks, converts the scanned image of a typed or printed page into text that can be edited.
la: What is a computer? Draw/describe the block diagram of a computer and explain the functions of its units.

A computer is a device that transforms data into meaningful information; it accepts, stores, processes and retrieves data and gives results. Block diagram: Input unit → Memory unit ↔ ALU, all under the Control Unit → Output unit. (1) Input unit — enters data and instructions (keyboard, mouse). (2) Memory unit — stores data and instructions. (3) ALU — arithmetic (add, subtract, multiply, divide), logic and comparison. (4) Control Unit — supervises all operations step by step; decides when to start and stop receiving data and where to store it. (5) Output unit — gives the results as useful information (monitor, printer). ALU + CU = CPU, the brain of the computer.

or: What is an input device? Describe any four input devices.

Input devices accept data and instructions from the user. (1) Keyboard — the most common, QWERTY layout, about 104 keys. (2) Mouse — hand-held pointing device to select, move and open items by point and click. (3) Light pen — selects objects by pointing directly at the screen. (4) Scanner — converts printed pages and pictures into electronic form; bar-code readers and OCR are scanners. Also touch screen, microphone and track ball.

la: What is software? Discuss its categories.

Software is a set of programs that makes the hardware perform tasks in a particular order. (1) System software runs the computer and manages its resources: the operating system (Windows, Linux, UNIX) provides the user interface and manages hardware and files; utilities (antivirus, zip, split/join) fill the gap between the OS and users' needs. (2) Application software does specific jobs: generalized packages (MS-Word, MS-Excel, PowerPoint, MS-Access, Photoshop) and customized packages made for an organisation (payroll, inventory, student information). Software is written in computer languages and translated by compilers and assemblers.
